authority: User continuation authorizes native host checks, isolated engineering fixtures on existing authorized Linux resources, and regression attribution. R4b remains paused.

starting_evidence.interpretation: Current continuation baseline, not a new native-host or process reliability result.

status_rules.passed: All required observations for the named case, exact host/platform and tested scope have raw evidence.
status_rules.failed: An executed applicable check contradicts a required invariant. Preserve original logs even after a corrected rerun.
status_rules.not_run: The check was not attempted; name the missing evidence and do not infer success from another check.
status_rules.blocked: A concrete prerequisite prevents execution, such as absent CLI, unavailable existing authorization, inaccessible authorized Linux, or unsupported platform. Preserve the actual failed attempt separately.
status_rules.partial_scope: Report subcase statuses separately. One host, capability or platform does not certify the others.
status_rules.cost: Preserve actual known usage, failed attempts, and outstanding reservations. Unavailable billing or overhead is null/unknown; quote is not measurement.

shared_evidence_requirements: Exact command, working directory, executable path and version, source/package hash and actual imported module paths.
Run identifiers, UTC or explicitly zoned timestamps, exit status and application status separately.
Raw structured host/process logs, actual tool requests and responses, fixture inputs and output hashes, relevant receipts and ledger before/after.
Record fixture executor identity and every injected failure. Real OS processes plus synthetic scientific output remain engineering fixtures.
Preserve original attempts and diagnostic failures. A retry is a new attempt linked to its predecessor, never an overwrite.
Do not collect credentials or full ambient environment dumps.
No writes to PRISM, historical science evidence, shared source/environment, old scientific jobs, or global host configuration.
No new cloud resources, WSL installation, shared dependency upgrades, R4b restart, paid scientific tasks, CRO orders, auto-commit or push.

host_protocol.entry: The actual official native CLI launches or connects the ETALON MCP configuration in an isolated project. A Python MCP client is not the native host.

supply: A bounded engineering task goal and fixture inputs.
Available resource and filesystem scope, cost/termination limits, and scientific pause boundary.
A short normal host guide and discoverable optional methods.
do_not_supply: A complete ordered list of calls or a fixed successor DAG.
A required choice of every skill or a full injection of all method content.
Fabricated tool results, predefined success text, or assertions that the host must claim improvement.
prompt_policy.feedback_policy: A fixture can intentionally reveal a contradiction, missing support or changed result through an actual executed tool response. Preserve that response and the subsequent visible decision. Do not inject a scripted instruction that merely tells the host which next method to select.
prompt_policy.selection_boundary: This protocol checks observable capability and bounded response to feedback, not superiority of phi, S, G, internal reasoning quality or scientific discovery.

required: The named native CLI executable/version and invocation are recorded.
The native run discovers the actual ETALON MCP surface and makes at least one substantive successful supported call with auditable output.
Raw host/tool logs bind the call to the actual server/package version and isolated fixture.
insufficient: Configuration existence, export verification, an MCP server launched alone, or a Python protocol client.
Exit code zero or narrative claims without an observable tool request and response.

required: A native run performs a substantive supported ETALON operation without adopting a method first.
Where ActionRequest is used, method_use_refs is empty and the same authoritative execution/receipt path is used.
Output, execution state, verification and admission are interpreted at their actual levels.
subcases.interpretation: A successful substantive read/validation operation establishes direct tool freedom only. It does not replace ACT-01 scientific-action execution. An unsupported active execution honestly reported is blocked for that action, not a successful execution.

required: The native host can discover and selectively read relevant content without loading every skill.
Partial use and composition are represented by actual method references and visible bounded choices; evaluate each exercised behavior separately.
A local method outside the six-entry catalog can be read or tried within authorization without mandatory promotion.
If the host modifies a reference or script, actual bytes/manifest identity change and the old snapshot remains addressable.
subcases.interpretation: Server returning bytes proves a read, not full adoption. Record a host-reported adoption as host_reported. Only directly witnessed script/action behavior receives its specific tool-observed description; do not assert that all private reasoning followed the skill.

required: An actual tool response supplies information relevant to the task.
The visible next behavior uses that information to add an unplanned step, change method/scope, or stop with a reason.
The changed behavior is within original authority and budget; a clear unsupported or insufficient-evidence stop is valid.
References connect the feedback output, subsequent choice and resulting action or stop.
insufficient: Claiming a change only in a final paragraph with no corresponding subsequent action or explicit stop.
Treating failure, unsupported operation or NOT_APPLICABLE as a zero scientific value.
Calling an unsupported operation through shell as a way around the same permission/capability boundary.

host_protocol.success_aggregation: Report all subcases for Codex and Claude Code independently. HOST-01 for a host is passed only for the explicitly exercised required capability set; missing composition/modification/adaptation is not silently inferred. Failure or absence of one host does not block reporting other completed engineering work.

entry: Read-only verification of an already authorized Linux host, actual interpreter and relevant active tasks precedes an isolated fixture run.
Use a new immutable source/package snapshot and new fixture workspace. Record module paths and hashes; do not overwrite shared environments or old jobs.

Use real separate processes and native OS locking/process identity. Do not replace the lock with nullcontext, replace worker launch with an in-process callback, or emulate process existence in the acceptance run.
A synthetic executor with deterministic non-scientific outputs and a durable invocation counter is permitted and must be identified as such.
Only fixture-owned PIDs and verified start identities/process groups may receive signals. Unrelated tasks remain untouched.

cases.intervention: Start two independent submitter processes against the same campaign with funds sufficient for only one quoted action, or with a single remaining replicate slot. Use an explicit barrier so the competing attempts overlap. Also check a pre-existing pending execution.
required: Real OS locks and authoritative SQLite reservation transactions remain active.
Only a legal affordable execution combination is dispatched; the loser receives busy/conflict/budget or equivalent explicit rejection.
No duplicated invocation for the same request, no negative available balance caused by double reservation, and no silent pending cleanup.
Invocation counter, job/action identities, reservation rows and ledger snapshots agree.
Separate request IDs cannot bypass a held pending attempt or an exhausted replicate cap.
cases.failure: Two incompatible executions run, reservation/fee facts are lost, or concurrency is made to pass by bypassing locks.
cases.bound: Report the actual number of races and schedules. Finite concurrency checks do not prove every possible interleaving.

cases.intervention: Let a real fixture worker execute and durably expose its completion evidence, then interrupt or lose the controller response before admission or acknowledgement. Start a separate status/reconcile process against the same job.
required: The durable observer/receipt and original action/job/process identities are retained.
Status/reconcile reads the original evidence and never starts a replacement scientific execution.
Invocation count remains one; failure costs and actual measured fixture cost remain charged exactly once.
Before sufficient completion evidence is available the state is unresolved/running and its reservation is retained.
When original evidence proves completion, admission and settlement occur through the existing validation path, preserving any rejection.
cases.unknown_variant: If completion evidence truly cannot be recovered, remaining unresolved with the reservation and a concrete recovery reason is the correct outcome; it is not a successful completion claim.
cases.failure: A lost response becomes an automatic new execution, unknown becomes zero/success, or reconciliation invents completion.

cases.intervention: Issue cancellation while a fixture child is verifiably active, including a child that delays or does not immediately honor the initial signal. Observe states before and after verified process exit.
required: PID plus start identity/process-group binding identify the fixture process, not merely a reusable PID.
Cancellation request and confirmed termination are distinct facts.
While an owned child is alive or its state is unknown, do not report cancelled or release the unresolved reservation.
After confirmed exit, preserve known costs and explain the resulting terminal or unresolved state using actual receipts.
Signals and cleanup affect only fixture-owned verified processes; cancellation/reconcile replay never respawns work.
cases.failure: Premature cancelled/refund, signal to an unverified or unrelated process, or hiding unknown child state.
cases.bound: Record timeout and escalation behavior actually exercised; do not infer other operating systems or external scheduler semantics.

regression_attribution.scope: Original A 32 failures and B 5 sklearn-related failures are identified individually; original outputs remain preserved.
required: Map original test IDs and error signatures to environment/platform, introduced regression, or pre-existing defect with source evidence.
Reproduce only relevant discriminating cases in the actual applicable environment; a skip/deselect is not a fix.
If source changes, preserve original failure, unique owner, minimal change, source hash and targeted rerun.
If dependency or platform remains unavailable, report blocked/not_run for the missing environment and failed for the actual unsuccessful attempt.
Do not install or upgrade a shared dependency merely to turn the report green.
Do not weaken correctness assertions, overwrite historical results, or count overlapping test groups as independent added coverage.

scientific_boundary.new_scientific_evaluation: not authorized by this engineering protocol
scientific_boundary.phi_S_G_benefit: not established by host or POSIX engineering checks
scientific_boundary.known_old_test_labels: remain seen; never reclassified as independent unseen evaluation
